figures.finding: The national government levies a wage and salary tax and a gross revenue tax on business, half of each shared with the states: wages and salaries bear 6% on the first $11,000 a year and 10% above (FSM Code tit. 54 § 121), withheld by the employer as paid and remitted quarterly; an employee earning under $5,000 a year may claim a $1,000 deduction by refund (§ 122); a business's gross revenue, a freelancer's fees and royalties included, bears $80 on the first $10,000 a year and 3% above, none at $2,000 or less (§§ 112(5), 141), paid quarterly.
figures.applies: Wage earners and businesses; the rates as the FSM Code (2014 codification, these sections last amended by PL 5-84) states them, read 2026-11-03.

figures.finding: Social Security tax is 7.5% of taxable wages from the worker and 7.5% from the employer (15% combined), on wages up to $7,000 a quarter; a self-employed person with no employees and over $10,000 of gross revenue reports quarterly wages for himself of 5% of the year's gross revenue and pays the 15% on them (with employees, twice the highest-paid employee's wages).
figures.applies: From 1 January 2013 (the statutory rise from 7% to 7.5% each); the quarterly base as FSMSSA states it ("currently").

sources.said: The statutory SS tax rate increase would increase the employee’s share of contributions from 7% to 7.5% of taxable wages and would also increase the employer’s matching contribution by the same rate, for a total of 2% increase in the combined SS tax rate (15%).
Currently the maximum quarterly taxable wage base is $7,000.
If gross revenues exceed $10,000, then these self-employed persons must report gross wages for themselves for each calendar quarter equal to 5% of the business’ gross revenues for the calendar year.
Quarterly Social Security Tax Due = $800 x 15% = $120.00
Self-employed persons with employees must report gross wages for themselves equal to twice the wages of the highest paid employee reported by them for that quarter.

figures.finding: Wages and salaries bear 6% on the first $11,000 a year and 10% above, withheld by the employer as paid and remitted with a quarterly return by 30 April, 31 July, 31 October and 31 January; an employee earning under $5,000 a year claims a $1,000 deduction by refund. A business's gross revenue (a freelancer's fees and royalties included) bears $80 a year on its first $10,000 and 3% above, none at $2,000 or less, paid with quarterly returns on the same dates. Wages for work done partly outside the FSM are presumed earned there, and an employee of an employer with no place of business or agent in the FSM files and pays the tax himself.

value.returns: quarterly, by 30 April, 31 July, 31 October and 31 January (§§ 132, 143); no annual return for an employee
value.nonResident: wages for work in and out of the FSM presumed FSM-sourced (§ 124); an employee of an employer with no FSM place of business or agent files and pays himself (§ 137); a non-employee's fees and royalties are a business's gross revenue (§ 112(5)); whether the wage tax withheld is final is not stated
value.authors: royalties and fees are a business's gross revenue (§ 112(5)); no separate rule

sources.title: FSM Code, Title 54, Chapter 1: Taxation of Wages, Salaries, and Gross Revenues (Legal Information System of the Federated States of Micronesia, the FSM Supreme Court its local executing agency)
sources.said: 121 . Tax on wages and salaries . There shall be assessed, levied, collected, and paid a tax of six percent upon the first $11,000 and ten percent upon the amount over the first $11,000 of all wages and salaries received by every employee, as defined, except as provided in section 122 of this chapter. … 122 . (1) Every employee, as defined, except those whose gross annual wages and salaries are $5,000 or more, shall be allowed a deduction of $1,000 per year … (2) The deduction shall be claimed by the employee filing for a refund … 124 . Source of wages . If an employee is credited or paid salaries or wages derived from, or attributable to, personal services performed or rendered both within and without the Federated States of Micronesia, then the whole of the salaries or wages shall be presumed to have been earned within the Federated States of Micronesia. … 132 . (1) The employer shall, on or before the last day of the month following the close of each quarter, to wit, on or before April 30, July 31, October 31, and January 31, pay the tax withheld … 137 . (1) Any individual who is paid or credited wages or salaries from an employer who does not have a place of business in the Federated States of Micronesia and does not have an agent within the Federated States of Micronesia … shall file a return with and pay the tax due … 141 . (1) There shall be assessed, levied, collected, and paid a tax of $80 per year upon that portion of the amount of gross revenues earned by every business subject to the provisions of this chapter which does not exceed $10,000 per year. (2) … a tax of three percent per year upon that portion … which is in excess of $10,000 per year. (3) Businesses which earn gross revenues of not more than $2,000 per year are exempt from taxation under this section. … 112 (5) Gross revenue means the gross receipts … received as compensation for personal services not in the form of salaries or wages … including interest, rentals, royalties, fees, or other emoluments however designated
